passages.text:
Re: Follow-up on Meta TPP Internews Report?
[contact omitted] Ulvi Ismayil Tuesday, April 30, 2024 at 10:28:14 PM Eastern Daylight Time
To: [contact omitted] Vera Zakem
Cc: [contact omitted] Cara Thanassi, [contact omitted] Chioma Ayogu, [contact omitted] Carrie Mitchell,
[contact omitted] Chantal Agarwal, [contact omitted] Daniella Burgi-Palomino, [contact omitted] Drusilla
Menaker, [contact omitted] Gary Bland, [contact omitted] Kayla Goodson, [contact omitted] Lorri Anne Meils,
[contact omitted] Susan Abbott
Hi Daniella et al,
All I remember from that meeting and further conversations with Internews is that Meta broke its ties with Internews when
this report was published. Internews even noticed that some NGOs that were previously in a coalition with Internews
stopped answering emails. I'm not surprised that Meta's reaction to that question was short.
Best regards,
Ulvi Ismayil,
Senior Media Advisor
USAID | Washington, DC
Bureau for Democracy, Human Rights, and Governance (DRG)
[opaque block]
[contact omitted]
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 8:52 PM Vera Zakem <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks Cara! Just from Agency perspective,1 am not comfortable in pressing on this further at this time.
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 4:44 PM Cara Thanassi <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks Chioma et al- we'll certainly loop in GC as LAC considers next steps on this.
Cara L. Thanassi
Democracy Specialist for Latin America and the Caribbean
USAID Bureau for Latin America and the Caribbean, Democracy and Human Rights Team
Cell: [opaque block]
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 6:39 PM Chioma Ayogu <[contact omitted]>wrote:
ATTORNEY CLIENT PRIVILEGED
I would also add that with respect to ongoing discussions with Meta or others, USAID will need to continue to tread
carefully and continue to ensure that it is not and is not perceived to be putting pressure on them to change
policies. My understanding is that USAID has already asked about issues with the program and received answers
from Meta. If USAID is not asking new questions or presenting new undiscussed issues the risk that USAID's
repeated pointed questions about the same program may be viewed as coercive. Further, the talking points for
such discussions would need to be carefully reviewed by GC to make sure they do not cross legal redlines.
These types of discussions should be conducted consistent with FAQ #16 of the GC guidance.
Warm regards,
Chioma
CHIOMA AYOGU
Senior Counsel
Office of the General Counsel, Development, Democracy and Economics (GC/DDE)
Clients: DRG Bureau
[contact omitted]

Phone: [opaque block]
U.S. Agency for International Development
1300 Pennsylvania Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20523
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 3:10 PM Chioma Ayogu <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks for looping me in, Vera. I would be happy to review. Also happy to chat, if helpful.
Best.
Chioma
CHIOMA AYOGU
Senior Counsel
Office of the General Counsel, Development, Democracy and Economics (GC/DDE)
Clients: DRG Bureau
[contact omitted]
Phone: [opaque block]
U.S. Agency for International Development
1300 Pennsylvania Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20523
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 3:04 PM Vera Zakem <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Attorney Client Privileged
I am adding Chioma to this thread. I think this request and review should be reviewed by GC in accordance to
the guidance that we (Agency, IRC, not DRG are issuing on this).
I'd like Chioma to connect with folks before you all proceed further. This is why I have not pushed on this
issue.
thanks, vera
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 3:02 PM Cara Thanassi <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Just weighing in here. From the LAC side of the house, we plan to review the report again, identify LAC
specific issues, and have a follow up conversation with them regarding any concrete actions they have
taken as a result of the report or plan to take. From the report, I would be reluctant to recommend
organizations participate in the TPP.
However, since this is a global issue, having a common agenda on this driven by the DRG Bureau in
collaboration with the regional bureaus would be useful and likely more effective.
Thanks,
Cara
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 2:55 PM Vera Zakem <[contact omitted]> wrote:
No. We have not.
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 2:50 PM Daniella Burgi-Palomino <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi colleagues,
Just following up to see whether there has been any further follow-up with Meta from the DRG Bureau
on the Trusted Partners Program (TPP) and how they are addressing/ have addressed the
recommendations outlined in the Internews report since this August 2023 call. Happy to schedule a cal
if that's easier. Just let me know. Thanks!
Best,
Daniella
On Wed, Apr 24, 2024 at 5:20 PM Daniella Burgi-Palomino <[contact omitted]>wrote:
Hi colleagues,

A few of us in LAC and Vera had a meeting with Meta's Sandra Luff, and Public Policy Managers for
South and Central America/ Mexico on April 9th (notes here). We asked them about how they
responded to the challenges identified in the Internews report related to the Trusted Partners
Program (TPP) and you can see their (brief) response in the notes. I know our old colleague Josh
Machleder once organized a call last August (invite below) with Internews on the report that some of
us joined but we were wondering if there had been any further follow-up with Meta from the DRG
Bureau on the TPP and how they are addressing/ have addressed the recommendations outlined in
the Internews report since this August 2023 call.
Please let us know if and/ or if you prefer to organize a brief call on this to discuss, feel free to let me
know who should join and I can look for a time next week. We'd like to know as we consider any
follow-up from our recent meeting with them. Many thanks!
Best,
Daniella
